questions.question: In causal_mask(4), which positions remain finite in row i=2?
options: Columns 0, 1, and 2
Only column 2
Columns 2 and 3
All four columns
questions.explanation: The mask sets 0.0 when j<=i and -inf otherwise, so row 2 can attend to its prefix through column 2.

questions.question: Which target does cross_entropy_shifted compare with logits_per_pos[i]?
options: target_ids[i]
target_ids[i+1]
target_ids[i-1] for every i
The most frequent target in the sequence
questions.explanation: The next-token loop runs to len(target_ids)-1 and explicitly indexes target_ids[i+1].

questions.question: What does sample_top_k(logits, k=3, ...) do before sampling?
options: It selects the third-largest ID deterministically
It keeps three random IDs and copies their original probabilities without renormalizing
It keeps the three largest logits, applies softmax to those values, and samples among their IDs
It removes the three most probable IDs and samples the remainder
questions.explanation: The function sorts logits descending, retains the first k, softmaxes the retained logits, and maps the sampled local index back to its vocabulary ID.

questions.question: How does temperature t=2.0 affect the logits before sample_temperature draws?
options: It adds 2.0 to every probability after softmax
It multiplies each logit by 2, making the distribution sharper
It keeps only the top two vocabulary entries
It divides each logit by 2, flattening the resulting distribution
questions.explanation: softmax(logits, temperature=t) divides logits by t; values above one reduce relative contrasts.

questions.question: What distinguishes top-p sampling from top-k sampling in this implementation?
options: Top-p keeps the smallest probability prefix whose cumulative mass reaches p, rather than a fixed number of IDs
Top-p always keeps exactly p vocabulary entries
Top-p chooses the largest logit and ignores all probabilities
Top-p applies a causal mask to the vocabulary indices
questions.explanation: sample_top_p sorts probabilities, stops when cumulative mass reaches p, renormalizes the retained prefix, and samples from it.

questions.question: Why is the trained-ish loss in demo_ce_loss expected to be below the random baseline ln(10)?
options: The code removes one of the ten classes from the denominator
Each position's next-token logit is boosted by 2.0, increasing its target probability relative to random logits
The shifted loss compares every position with its own input, making it zero
Random logits are sampled with a negative temperature
questions.explanation: The demo adds 2.0 to the correct next-token logit for each training target, so its negative log probability should improve over unbiased random logits.
